clue.text: Young woman cut with it?

indicators.note: cut says the word loses its tail letter

parts.note: chick is slang for a young woman

explanation.surface: A teenager asks whether she is fashionable once she has had her hair cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the K from CHICK. The question mark flags 'with it' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being 'with it' means fashionably up to date, which is what stylish means.

clue.text: Turn in drama (time for 27 shock)

indicators.note: time for 27 means the letter standing for time replaces the one standing for 27-down
in puts the turn letter inside the word drama

parts.note: taken as written
a U-turn, so turn gives U
27 is the answer to 27-down, abbreviated D as in calendar notation

explanation.surface: A twist in a play delivers a shock to the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts U into DRAMA, giving DRAUMA; 'time for 27' swaps T in for D, the abbreviation of 27-down's answer, date.
explanation.definitionFit: Trauma is a severe emotional shock, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Freedom to use land is why fair got in a mess?

indicators.note: in a mess says these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A walker asks why a fair has been allowed to churn up a public footpath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a mess' rearranges WHY FAIR GOT. The question mark hints that the fair got into a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A right of way is a legal entitlement to pass over someone else's ground.

clue.text: On North by Northwest, upset over one late director

indicators.note: over says the turned letters sit over, around, the letter for one
upset in a down clue turns the run of letters upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: on in the sense of concerning gives RE
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A film buff comments on a late director overturning ideas about North by Northwest, Hitchcock's thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses RENNW to WNNER, and 'over' wraps it round I. Michael Winner was an English film director who died in 2013.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Winner was a British film director, now dead, best known for Death Wish.

clue.text: Spot for murderers — each cast supporting director

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue puts the following pieces beneath the letter for director

parts.note: to cast is to throw

explanation.surface: Every member of a film's cast backs the director in a crime movie about killers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' puts EA + THROW underneath D.
explanation.definitionFit: Condemned killers awaiting execution are held in the cells known by this name.

clue.text: Smudge cosmetic she took away

indicators.note: took away says the word she is removed from the cosmetic

parts.note: blusher is a cosmetic for colouring the cheeks
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman removes her makeup and leaves a smudge behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took away' removes SHE from BLUSHER, leaving the letters on either side.
explanation.definitionFit: A blur and a smudge are both indistinct smears, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Rude, single Hitchcock lead actor, working over breaks

parts.note: single means one, the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: breaks says the turned word splits the actor's name

parts.note: Cary Grant starred in several Hitchcock films, such as North by Northwest

indicators.note: over says the word for working is turned round

parts.note: on means working, as of a machine

explanation.surface: An unmarried star of Hitchcock's films is rude while working on set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the word for working round, and 'breaks' splits the actor's name after its first letter. 'Hitchcock lead actor' points to Cary Grant.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially, ignorant describes someone discourteous or ill-mannered, i.e. rude.

clue.text: Alien, like foreign characters

parts.note: ET is the alien of the Spielberg film
as means like, in comparisons

explanation.surface: An alien behaves like the strange characters in a foreign film.
explanation.definitionFit: Etas are letters of the Greek alphabet, characters from a foreign script.

clue.text: Having no preference in bedroom, police enter here, finding killer in bed

indicators.note: enter says the police and the other piece go inside the word here

parts.note: taken as written
BI, short for bisexual, describes someone attracted to either sex
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Detectives burst into a bedroom and discover a murderer lying in the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enter' sends the bisexual and the detectives into the word here. The definition's 'bed' is a flower bed, not the bedroom's, and the killer is a weedkiller.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbicide kills weeds, so it is a killer used in a garden bed.

clue.text: See 25
See 22
Well-known American after Olympics rejection?

indicators.note: after says the American abbreviation follows the rejection

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Olympics; rejecting it is saying no to Rio

explanation.surface: An American becomes famous after losing out on an Olympic bid.
explanation.walkthrough: Hitchcock's Notorious is one of the puzzle's film themes.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious means widely known, usually for something bad, a stronger synonym of famous.

clue.text: Magnetism in girl's case — illicit affair to follow

indicators.note: to follow says the affair comes after the girl's outer letters
the case of the word girl is its outside pair of letters

parts.note: an amour is a secret love affair

explanation.surface: A girl's legal case is made more alluring by a scandalous affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' keeps only the outside letters of GIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour is alluring attractiveness, a kind of personal magnetism.

clue.text: Feel good with Hitchcock film

parts.note: Rope is a 1948 Hitchcock thriller

explanation.surface: A cinema-goer feels good after watching a Hitchcock classic.
explanation.definitionFit: To grope is to feel about with the hands, searching blindly.

clue.text: Present differently — concerned with shot on film

parts.note: re means concerning or about
a frame is a single image on a strip of film

explanation.surface: An editor reworks a film, concerned with one shot.
explanation.definitionFit: To reframe an issue is to set it out from a new angle, presenting it another way.

clue.text: Shoots on outings series of pictures

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: to shoot a scene is to film it
trips are outings

explanation.surface: A photographer takes shots on day trips, building a sequence of pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A filmstrip is a length of film holding a sequence of still images for projection.

clue.text: Watching, say, dark force stabbing

indicators.note: stabbing says the dark force pierces into the abbreviation for say

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated EG
yin is the dark, passive principle of Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: Someone observes a sinister power plunging in a knife, perhaps in a thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: Eying is a spelling of eyeing, looking at closely, a synonym of watching.

clue.text: Stock producer holding black and white cattle's collar

indicators.note: holding says the stock producer contains the letter for black

parts.note: Oxo is a British brand of stock cubes
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A livestock breeder keeps black and white cows wearing collars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks like livestock, but OXO is a British stock-cube brand used for gravy.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxbow is the U-shaped wooden collar that goes round an ox's neck in a yoke.

clue.text: Fetching ones start to become identical (they are)

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the word become

parts.note: ringers, as in dead ringers, are things that are identical to each other

explanation.surface: Attractive people start to look the same, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fetching' reads as attractive but means carrying something along.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringers are those who bring, i.e. those who fetch things.

clue.text: Watched horror film

definitions.meaning: past tense of see, meaning observed
the 2004 horror movie about Jigsaw's deadly traps

explanation.surface: A filmgoer saw a scary movie.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past tense of see and the title of a 2004 horror film.

clue.text: The Guardian writers mostly set without expectation

indicators.note: without in its sense of outside says the shortened word wraps round the rest
mostly says the word set loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
the Guardian refers to itself as we, so its writers give US
pens are writing instruments

explanation.surface: The newspaper's staff are largely resigned to having no hopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, so the shortened set goes round everything else. A paper speaking of itself says 'we', hence 'us'.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the tense anticipation of waiting for what will happen.

clue.text: "Some characters to kill at …" — Hitchcock getting stick

indicators.note: some characters means a run of letters taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A quotation about murder leads to Hitchcock getting beaten with a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: The lathi is an Indian iron-bound bamboo stick, carried notably by police in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathi is a long heavy stick used as a weapon in South Asia.

clue.text: "Furious" women from Italy and Spain crossing New York (Queens borders)

indicators.note: borders says the queens go round everything else

parts.note: ER is the abbreviation for a queen, Elizabeth Regina, so queens are ERS

indicators.note: crossing says the two country letters straddle the New York abbreviation

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Angry women travel from Southern Europe to New York, on the outskirts of the borough of Queens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' sets the city between the two country letters; 'borders' wraps the queens round all of it. Queens looks like the New York borough but means royal women.
explanation.definitionFit: The Erinyes are the Furies of Greek myth, avenging female spirits.

clue.text: A snug Hitchcock stripped off — work for it here?

indicators.note: off says the letters are thrown into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: stripped says the director's name loses its outside letters

explanation.surface: A cosy Hitchcock, undressed, suggests something seedy about getting film roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped' leaves ITCHCOC from HITCHCOCK; 'off' rearranges it with A SNUG. The question mark marks the definition as indirect.
explanation.definitionFit: A casting couch is where actors are notoriously pressured into sexual favours in return for parts.

clue.text: "See you on Twitter?" — blue post of priest

parts.note: CU is text-speak shorthand for see you
blue means risqué or racy

explanation.surface: A clergyman signs off a smutty social-media message.
explanation.definitionFit: A curacy is the office or position held by a curate, an assistant cleric.

clue.text: Dressed and working

definitions.meaning: functioning, like a vehicle engaged with its gearbox

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means clothed in kit and also operating, like an engaged engine.

clue.text: Clobber for going off with … : anger flows

indicators.note: flows says the letters run freely into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone leaving in a temper is clothed, with fury pouring out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' is British slang for clothes, and 'going off' means dropping off to sleep, not storming out.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyjamas and nightgowns are clothes worn to sleep in, i.e. for dropping off.

clue.text: Tone reflects section of The Lady Vanishes

indicators.note: reflects says the hidden letters are read backwards
section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A shade of colour mirrors part of Hitchcock's film The Lady Vanishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Navy is a dark blue shade, one tone of colour.

clue.text: Part of American car seen in Rear Window

parts.note: tail means the back or rear
a light is a pane of a window

explanation.surface: A US car appears in Hitchcock's film Rear Window.
explanation.definitionFit: Taillight is the American term for the red lamp at the back of a vehicle.

clue.text: Was in Frenzy in which director ultimately matured

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of the word director

parts.note: aged means matured, as cheese or wine

explanation.surface: A director grew up while making Hitchcock's film Frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: Frenzy is a 1972 Hitchcock film, but here it simply means a fury.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a frenzy is to be in a wild fury, which is how someone behaves who stormed.

clue.text: '50s hairstyle and its wearer clipped to go out

parts.note: the DA, duck's arse, was a swept-back 1950s hairstyle

indicators.note: clipped says the wearer's name loses its last letter

parts.note: the Teddy boys or Teds of 1950s Britain favoured that hairstyle

explanation.surface: A man with a 1950s quiff gets a haircut before a night on the town.
explanation.walkthrough: A Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style suits; 'clipped' trims him to TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To go out with someone is to date them romantically.

clue.text: He noted essentially: "See Kim Novak in disguise across road"

indicators.note: across says the jumbled letters straddle the abbreviation for road
in disguise says those central letters appear in another order
essentially means the central letter of each of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: A man remarked that Kim Novak, disguised in Vertigo, should be watched crossing a street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes E, I and V from See, Kim and Novak; 'in disguise' rearranges them as VEI, and 'across' puts it round RD. Novak's character in Vertigo wears a disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was a composer, a man who wrote down notes.

clue.text: One crawling out of Psycho shot with worker

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so the film title is broken up

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: Someone creeps out of a screening of Hitchcock's Psycho with a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crawling' means fawning, not creeping on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant fawns on people of influence, the sense of crawling as toadying.
